description: PowerShell cmdlet to retrieve UDP endpoint information including local address and port bindings.
prerequisites: Admin privileges for full endpoint details

flags.purpose: Filter UDP endpoints by local IP address.
flags.security_use_case: Find services bound to specific interfaces on multi-homed systems.
flags.threat_detected: Services unexpectedly bound to external interfaces.
flags.safe_followup: Review service binding and firewall rules.

flags.purpose: Filter UDP endpoints by local port number.
flags.security_use_case: Identify services listening on specific UDP ports like DNS (53) or NTP (123).
flags.threat_detected: Unexpected UDP listeners potentially indicating malware or backdoors.
flags.safe_followup: Identify owning process and verify legitimacy.

flags.purpose: Show UDP endpoints owned by a specific process ID.
flags.security_use_case: Correlate UDP listening to specific services or malware.

powerful_combinations.why_powerful: Finds non-standard UDP listeners that may indicate malware.
powerful_combinations.security_context: Detect backdoors or unauthorized services using UDP.

powerful_combinations.command: Get-NetUDPEndpoint | ForEach-Object { Get-Process -Id $_.OwningProcess -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue } | Where-Object {$_.Path -notmatch 'C:\Windows'} | Select-Object Name,Path
powerful_combinations.why_powerful: Identifies processes with UDP endpoints running from outside System32.
powerful_combinations.security_context: Detect rogue processes listening on UDP ports.

powerful_combinations.why_powerful: Finds UDP endpoints bound to non-loopback addresses.
powerful_combinations.security_context: Identify services exposed on network interfaces.
